ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Fisher z-transformation absent — must know this is required for meta-analytic pooling of r
ground_truth.original_snippet: The rma function converted effect size r to Fisher’s z for the calculations, and we converted z back to effect size r for reporting of results (Borenstein, et al., 2009).
ground_truth.description: Deleted Fisher z-transformation step — meta-analysis on raw r is biased due to non-normal sampling distribution; reader can't verify computation was correct

matched_finding.subcategory: Meta-analysis of correlations using raw r rather than Fisher z not justified
matched_finding.description: The methods state that the rma function accepted effect size r and N parameters, suggesting correlations were meta-analyzed on the r scale. Standard practice is to transform correlations to Fisher's z for analysis and back-transform estimates, because the sampling variance of r is nonnormal and depends on the true correlation. Without clarification, the meta-analytic estimates, CIs, and heterogeneity statistics may be biased or incorrectly estimated.
matched_finding.quote: The rma function was used, which accepts the effect size r and N parameters

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Creates internal contradiction detectable within the paper
ground_truth.original_snippet: 80 for the present study as this was the sample size in the original study
ground_truth.modified_snippet: 120 for the present study to ensure adequate statistical power
ground_truth.description: Changed minimum N from 80 to 120, but Table 1 shows sites collected 80-90 participants — stated requirement not met

matched_finding.description: The manuscript states that all included studies met a CREP minimum sample size of 120, but later reports that included sample sizes ranged from 80 to 374, and Table 1 lists six of seven replications with N below 120. This contradiction matters because sample-size eligibility, power, and inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are unclear.
matched_finding.quote: All studies in this meta-analysis received this approval by the CREP team, collected the minimum number of participants specified by the CREP (120 for the present study to ensure adequate statistical power)

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Mean centering absent — must know this is needed for cross-study effect size comparison
ground_truth.original_snippet: The composite self-esteem score was mean centered in accord with the Forest and Wood (2012) analysis.
ground_truth.description: Deleted mean-centering step — essential for matching original analysis and comparing effect sizes across replications; without centering, beta coefficients are non-comparable

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Temporal context (2012 vs 2016) removed — must recognize historical change as alternative explanation
ground_truth.original_snippet: differences between the original and replication results might be related to changes in social media usage patterns from 2012 to 2016. By the time the replications occurred in 2016–17,
ground_truth.modified_snippet: differences between the original and replication results might be related to variations in social media usage patterns across populations.
ground_truth.description: Removed temporal framing (2012 vs 2016-17) — eliminates key alternative explanation that Facebook's social role changed historically, obscuring whether non-replication reflects fragile finding or genuine historical change

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Claims urban/suburban only but Table 1 shows rural institutions — cross-reference needed
ground_truth.original_snippet: in urban, suburban, and rural settings in the eastern, Midwest, and western U.S.,
ground_truth.modified_snippet: in urban and suburban settings in the eastern and western U.S.,
ground_truth.description: Removed 'rural' and 'Midwest' — contradicts actual institutional data in Table 1 (BYU-Idaho is rural); undermines generalizability argument

matched_finding.description: The manuscript emphasizes diverse institutions, but the sample remains limited to five U.S. colleges/universities and undergraduate psychology participant pools. Institutional variety does not solve demographic, cultural, and age restrictions.
matched_finding.quote: These CREP research teams represented five diverse institutions, both public and private, in urban and suburban settings in the eastern and western U.S.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Anderson & Maxwell adaptation detail removed — must know their method was for d not r
ground_truth.original_snippet: We adapted the method to use effect size r to estimate 95% CIs for the difference in effect sizes for each of the replications compared with the original study (Anderson & Maxwe
ground_truth.modified_snippet: We used the method to estimate 95% CIs for the difference in effect sizes for each of the replications compared with the original study (Anderson & Maxwe
ground_truth.description: Changed 'adapted the method to use effect size r' to 'used the method' — hides non-trivial adaptation of d-based method to r-family; reader can't evaluate validity

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Non-Facebook users included — must recognize this invalidates construct measurement
ground_truth.original_snippet: Five participants who were not Facebook users were excluded from analyses.
ground_truth.description: Deleted non-Facebook-user exclusion — including non-users invalidates construct measurement (rating a platform they don't use); biases effects toward zero

matched_finding.subcategory: No assessment of current Facebook use or eligibility
matched_finding.description: The manuscript does not report whether participants were required to be current Facebook users, how frequently they used Facebook, or whether non-users were excluded. Perceptions of Facebook self-disclosure and connection are difficult to interpret for participants who rarely use or do not use Facebook.
matched_finding.quote: participants completed a measure of Facebook use perceptions created by the original researchers

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Mechanism measurement caveat removed — must distinguish pattern consistency from mechanism testing
ground_truth.original_snippet: However, the CREP studies did not include a measure of FTF vs. online anxiety, making this an interesting direction for future research.
ground_truth.description: Deleted caveat that anxiety mechanism was not measured — paper now overclaims support for social compensation theory when it only found a consistent pattern, not the proposed mechanism

matched_finding.subcategory: Theory claim inconsistent with mixed/null findings
matched_finding.description: Social compensation theory is invoked even though the connection and expression outcomes—central to compensation—were weak, inconsistent, or opposite in direction. The theory discussion should be more constrained to disclosure safety/advantages perceptions.
matched_finding.quote: This theory suggests that for those with lower self-esteem, the anxiety provoked by FTF interactions can be somewhat mitigated in online interactions.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Creates internal contradiction detectable within the paper
ground_truth.original_snippet: We chose to use the restricted maximum likelihood (REML) model because it has been shown to exhibit less bias than the more commonly used DerSimonian and Laird (DL) model with small numbers of studies (Veroniki et al., 2016).
ground_truth.modified_snippet: We compared restricted maximum likelihood (REML) and DerSimonian and Laird (DL) models and selected REML as it produced more interpretable heterogeneity estimates for our data (Veroniki et al., 2016).
ground_truth.description: Changed principled REML selection (less bias with small k) to post-hoc model selection based on 'more interpretable' results — explicit analytic flexibility

matched_finding.description: The authors compared REML and DL estimators and selected REML because it produced 'more interpretable' heterogeneity estimates. Without a prespecified criterion, choosing between estimators after seeing results introduces analytic flexibility, especially with only seven studies where heterogeneity estimates are unstable.
matched_finding.quote: We compared restricted maximum likelihood (REML) and DerSimonian and Laird (DL) models and selected REML as it produced more interpretable heterogeneity estimates for our data

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Unknown missing data procedures acknowledged — must expect this transparency in multi-site studies
ground_truth.original_snippet: Contributors did not always post analysis scripts, so procedures to account for missing data are not known for all studies.
ground_truth.description: Deleted acknowledgment that missing data procedures are unknown for some studies — reader assumes uniform data handling when it actually varied

matched_finding.description: The authors acknowledge that some studies did not document missing-data handling, exclusions, or composite calculations. This is a serious reproducibility issue because correlations and Ns can vary depending on listwise versus pairwise deletion, exclusion rules, and scale scoring.
matched_finding.quote: not all studies posted analysis scripts or narratives to help us determine such things as missing data handling, composite score calculations, data exclusions, etc.
